text: 🇲🇽🔍 "How could one not be happy with these results?" "People in their neighborhood: from half saying they felt unsafe, to 35.9% today. And the trains are doing well, the highways are doing well, the water projects are doing well." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 INEGI's latest survey: the share of adults who feel unsafe in their own neighborhood or locality fell from 50.6% in 2018 to 35.9% in 2026, down 11.4% in the last year alone. Perceived insecurity in their municipality dropped from 70.3% in 2019 to 60.9%.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INFLATION 3.45% IN SEPTEMBER, BELOW FORECASTS; CORE AT LOWEST SINCE MARCH 2025</u>

INEGI reports annual inflation of 3.45% for September, up from 3.26% in August but less than analysts expected. Tomatoes (+30.25% in the month), onions (+23%) and LP gas drove the rise. Core inflation, the measure Banxico watches, fell from 3.88% to 3.75%, its lowest level since March 2025. Headline inflation stays inside Banxico's 2–4% band, and El Financiero reports open debate inside the central bank over whether to keep cutting rates.

🇲🇽✊ <u>CDMX REPLACES SHELTERS WITH "CARE COMMUNITIES" FOR 2,000 HOMELESS PEOPLE</u>

Clara Brugada's government presented "Una Nueva Mirada": four Comunidades de Cuidados with room for more than 2,000 people living on the street. The first opens in January 2027. Instead of crowded dormitories there will be small rooms, spaces where families can stay together, women-only areas, mental health and addiction care, free medicines, job training and a route to housing. Some will even let residents keep their pets.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>MILK AND MEDICINE FOR CUBA: NEW DRIVE AT THE MONUMENTO A LA REVOLUCIÓN</u>

While Washington seizes fuel shipments bound for the island, Mexicans are lining up again at the Monumento a la Revolución in Mexico City. The Colectivo Solidaridad Militante Va por Cuba opened its sixth collection drive for milk and medicines today. It runs through October 11, timed to the 59th anniversary of Che Guevara's death. Tons of aid donated by Mexican citizens have already been shipped to Cuba in recent months.
banner: CUBA: 6TH AID DRIVE IN MEXICO CITY

🇲🇽🔥 <u>SENATE VOTES 96–0 TO FINE BANKS FOR TELEPHONE HARASSMENT</u>

Mexico's Senate amended the Federal Consumer Protection Law so banks, insurers and other companies that keep calling people who have already said no face fines from 56,570 up to 2.4 million pesos. It passed 96 to 0. The reform bans repeated, unauthorized calls and ads through any channel. Truecaller data puts Mexico among the countries with the most unwanted calls, averaging 20 to 25 per user every month.
banner: PHONE SPAM: FINES UP TO 2.4M PESOS

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Car Production Fell 15.1% in September</u>

Mexico built 301,803 light vehicles in September, down 15.1% from 355,589 a year earlier, while auto exports fell 11.9%, according to INEGI data reported by El Financiero. From January to September, output is down 2.42% to 2,946,943 units and exports are down 1.50%. Mexicans themselves keep buying: domestic sales are up 5.03% over the same nine months.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Mexico Marches for Palestine, Three Years Into the Genocide in Gaza</u>

Collectives across Mexico have organized two days of action, October 7 and 10, demanding a ceasefire. In Mexico City, students marched from the Alameda Central to the former US embassy, and the Interuniversity and Popular Assembly for Palestine called a protest outside Israel's embassy. On Saturday, October 10, the Global March for Palestine takes over Mexico City at noon, Guadalajara at the Glorieta de los Desaparecidos at 4:30 pm, and Morelia's Jardín Morelos at 4:00 pm, under the slogan "For those who resist, the martyrs, and the Land."

text:
🇲🇽🏛️ <u>CNDH to Querétaro: We Never Banned School Backpack Checks</u>

Querétaro's education secretary, Martha Elena Soto Obregón, blamed a 2019 human rights recommendation for blocking the "Mochila Segura" backpack inspections in the state's schools. Mexico's National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) called that reading "unfounded": Recommendation 48/2019 does not prohibit the operation. It requires that inspections respect children's rights and the best interest of the child. The SEP already issued guidelines for safe school environments that let states design their own protocols, with voluntary checks carried out alongside parents.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Own Anti-Corruption Auditors Flag 592 Million Pesos in Scholarship Payments</u>

An audit by the Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Government found that the Benito Juárez scholarship program paid 592.3 million pesos in 2024 and 2025 to 67,142 students whose identities were never validated against the National Population Registry. It also found that Banco del Bienestar never delivered 95,960 cards in 2024, yet 94,251 of them showed as active. The finding is part of 5.639 billion pesos in irregularities across federal spending flagged in the 2025 audits.
